newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, potentially $1.00 higher on ideas extreme heat and humidity will continue to limit marketings, livestock dealers said.
Prices on Monday were $0.50 to $1.00 higher than Friday's, as hot, humid weather lingered over the Midwest after moving in on Saturday.
Hot, humid weather increase livestock stress, lower rates of gain and sometimes result in death loss, sources said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $60.50 to $61.00.
Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant were expected at $60.50 and Indiana/Ohio top hog prices were seen $61.00 to $61.50, sources in those areas said.
The extent of Tuesday's price strength depends on how many hogs are shipped overnight or in the early hours Tuesday morning, when temperatures and humidity should be more bearable, dealers said.
"If we get enough hogs early, we can probably keep prices steady, but if they don't come in, we could easily go up another $0.50, " a central Iowa hog buyer said.
